bug_semantics: getRecommendTitleFromMarkdownString synchronously applies /#{1,6} {1,}(.*\S.*)(?:\n|$)/g to Markdown supplied to the save/save-as path. For a heading prefix followed by a long run of spaces and a newline, the required non-space cannot match, while the adjacent space repetition and broad repetitions repeatedly repartition and rescan the same input. This causes approximately quadratic backtracking in the Electron main process and can freeze the application.
flaw_origin: PR #1281 changed the heading capture from (.+) to (.*\S.*) to reject whitespace-only headings. Its sole original member ba9865a0fc7df8052b3cdd1b928aaa28215bcb64 first wrote the vulnerable expression. The upstream landing object 15f8c7b2c57296370e06e743702101a11c2ac809 has the same parent and tree, so it is the squash carrier rather than the smallest BIC; later replay dee8bb6f5b8a8e19a6e117f673c93f9dcad4aae1 is likewise not the origin.
ai_marker: absent: git cat-file -p ba9865a0fc7df8052b3cdd1b928aaa28215bcb64 shows human author and committer Felix Häusler <hfelix@protonmail.ch> and only the message 'Fix recommend title exception when heading contains spaces only'; the BIC commit object contains no AI tool/model name, bot identity, Generated-with marker, Co-Authored-By trailer, or other AI attribution.
evidence: Introducer disagreement resolved: the primary selected ba9865a0fc7df8052b3cdd1b928aaa28215bcb64, while the reviewer selected upstream carrier 15f8c7b2c57296370e06e743702101a11c2ac809. git ls-remote origin refs/pull/1281/head resolves to ba9865a0fc7df8052b3cdd1b928aaa28215bcb64, and git rev-list --reverse 04480e08ae8987b50cd17e08844f742ca40635f7..ba9865a0fc7df8052b3cdd1b928aaa28215bcb64 returns that one member only. git cat-file -p on both candidates shows the identical parent 04480e08ae8987b50cd17e08844f742ca40635f7 and identical tree fd0cc1d0be89e71aaffcc34943de7165ff0b66b5. The primary therefore wins: ba9865a0fc7df8052b3cdd1b928aaa28215bcb64 is the recovered original member and 15f8c7b2c57296370e06e743702101a11c2ac809 is its upstream squash carrier, not the smallest BIC.

Direct parent check: git diff 04480e08ae8987b50cd17e08844f742ca40635f7 ba9865a0fc7df8052b3cdd1b928aaa28215bcb64 -- src/main/utils/index.js shows the causal replacement of (.+) by (.*\S.*). git show 04480e08ae8987b50cd17e08844f742ca40635f7:src/main/utils/index.js directly shows only /#{1,6} {1,}(.+)(?:\n|$)/g, so the immediate parent lacks the vulnerable mechanism.

Version boundary check: git diff v0.15.0 v0.15.1 -- src/main/utils/index.js shows the same causal replacement, establishing v0.15.1 as the first observed vulnerable tag. git show v0.19.1:packages/desktop/src/main/utils/index.ts, git show v0.20.0-rc.1:packages/desktop/src/main/utils/index.ts, and git show develop:packages/desktop/src/main/utils/index.ts all retain the vulnerable expression; develop resolves to e52106fd1cdcbd33c1258b7b0cdc7013c4c5d86c. The advisory's 'up to 0.17.1' wording is therefore not a patched boundary.

Fix disagreement resolved: both audits record fix_sha as null, but the primary records fork proposal c59b3ad423dfa082869933baf9f5d5c69bdcc560 as direct_fix_sha while the reviewer records null. git diff c59b3ad423dfa082869933baf9f5d5c69bdcc560^ c59b3ad423dfa082869933baf9f5d5c69bdcc560 shows a one-line (?! ) mitigation, but git ls-remote origin returns it only as refs/pull/3952/head and no refs/pull/3952/merge; GitHub's PR #3952 API reports state closed, merged_at null, and merge_commit_sha null; git branch --all --contains and git tag --contains return nothing. The reviewer wins this point: an unmerged fork proposal is evidence of a possible mitigation, not an upstream fix or direct member of an upstream fix, so both fix fields are null.

BIC-only AI check: the raw ba9865a0fc7df8052b3cdd1b928aaa28215bcb64 commit object contains human author/committer metadata, a signed ordinary bug-fix message, and no AI attribution. No PR-body, branch-name, later-refactor, or fix-only signal is used.
reasoning: The vulnerable failure mechanism begins at the semantic replacement of (.+) with (.*\S.*). The original PR head is available as a single commit and predates the same-parent, same-tree upstream carrier, so the protocol's smallest-real-BIC and reject-squash-aggregate rules require ba9865a0fc7df8052b3cdd1b928aaa28215bcb64, resolving the introducer disagreement in favor of the primary. Its immediate parent directly lacks the mechanism, and the vulnerable form begins between v0.15.0 and v0.15.1. The only proposed mitigation inspected is c59b3ad423dfa082869933baf9f5d5c69bdcc560, but it is a closed, unmerged fork PR and is contained by no upstream branch or tag; later release and develop trees remain vulnerable. Thus the reviewer is correct that it is not eligible for either fix field, making this an explicit unpatched case rather than a missing lifecycle check. Finally, the admissible AI evidence is only the recovered BIC commit object, which has no AI marker, so the gate-complete attribution verdict is NOT_AI.
remaining_gap: Upstream remains unpatched in the validated history through v0.20.0-rc.1 and develop e52106fd1cdcbd33c1258b7b0cdc7013c4c5d86c. There is therefore no upstream fix commit, decomposed direct fix member, or first fixed version; c59b3ad423dfa082869933baf9f5d5c69bdcc560 remains only a closed, unmerged fork proposal.
